blocks.text: To understand viscosity, stir water in a beaker with a glass rod and leave it; the swirling subsides after a while. Watching carefully, the liquid layer next to the walls comes to rest first and the layer near the centre stops last: the stationary layer at the walls slows the layer touching it, that slowed layer slows the next inner layer but to a lesser extent, and so a slow-moving layer of liquid tends to slow down the fast-moving layer next to it. This is a frictional force between adjacent layers.

blocks.title: Viscosity
blocks.text: This resistance to the flow of a liquid is termed viscosity. In the SI system its unit is kg per m per s; in the CGS system the unit is the poise (P).
